Record Class HeaderElement

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
io.micronaut.http.util.HeaderElement
Record Components:
value - The value before the first parameter, trimmed, as written (not unquoted)
parameters - The parameters in order of appearance; names are lower case, values unquoted. On a repeated name the first occurrence wins.
public record HeaderElement(String value, Map<String,String> parameters) extends Record
One element of an HTTP header value: a value followed by ;-separated parameters, as in text/html; charset="utf-8"; q=0.8 or form-data; name="file"; filename="a.txt".

The tokenizer follows the RFC 9110 list and parameter syntax: elements are separated by commas, parameters by semicolons, parameter values are tokens or quoted strings (with backslash escapes), and separators inside quoted strings or inside <...> (as in the Link header) are not delimiters. It is lenient: empty elements and parameters are skipped, a parameter without = has an empty value, and surrounding whitespace is trimmed.

Since:
5.3.0
Author:
Denis Stepanov

    • parseQualityOrderedList

      public static List<HeaderElement> parseQualityOrderedList(Iterable<? extends CharSequence> values)
      Parse the comma-separated lists of several values of the same header and order the elements by descending quality. Elements of equal quality keep their order; elements with a quality of 0 ("not acceptable") and elements with a malformed quality (see quality()) are dropped. Each quality is parsed once.
      Parameters:
      values - The header values
      Returns:
      The elements ordered by quality

    • quoteIfNeeded

      public static String quoteIfNeeded(CharSequence value)
      Quote a value if it is not a token (RFC 9110), escaping " and \. Characters that cannot appear in a quoted string (CR, LF, other control characters except HTAB, and characters above 0xFF) are rejected, so a value cannot split a header.
      Parameters:
      value - The value
      Returns:
      The value, or the quoted string
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If the value contains a character not allowed in a quoted string

    • quality

      public double quality()
      The quality value (q parameter): 1 when absent. The value is parsed strictly as an RFC 9110 qvalue (0[.ddd] or 1[.000]); anything else, such as .5, 5e-1 or 1.5, is malformed and yields 0, so the element is treated as not acceptable.
      Returns:
      The quality
